cases.sentence: Анатоль вышел из комнаты и через несколько минут вернулся в подпоясанной серебряным ремнем шубке и собольей шапке, молодцовато надетой на бекрень и очень шедшей к его ___.
cases.explain: «красивому лицу» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Anatole went out of the room and returned a few minutes later wearing a fur coat girt with a silver belt, and a sable cap jauntily set on one side and very becoming to his handsome face. Having looked in a mirror, and standing before Dólokhov in the same pose he had assumed before it, he lifted a glass of wine.

cases.sentence: Поглядевшись в зеркало и в той ___, которую он взял перед зеркалом, став перед Долоховым, он взял стакан вина.
cases.explain: «самой позе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Anatole went out of the room and returned a few minutes later wearing a fur coat girt with a silver belt, and a sable cap jauntily set on one side and very becoming to his handsome face. Having looked in a mirror, and standing before Dólokhov in the same pose he had assumed before it, he lifted a glass of wine.

cases.sentence: Красивая, худая и бледная цыганка, с блестящими, черными глазами и с черными, курчавыми сизого отлива волосами, в ___, выбежала с собольим салопом на руке.
cases.explain: «красной шали» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: A handsome, slim, and pale-faced gypsy girl with glittering black eyes and curly blue-black hair, wearing a red shawl, ran out with a sable mantle on her arm.

cases.sentence: — и он придвинул голову Анатоля к отверстию, оставленному воротником, из которого виднелась ___ Maтреши.
cases.explain: «блестящая улыбка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “That’s the way,” said Dólokhov, “and then so!” and he turned the collar up round her head, leaving only a little of the face uncovered. “And then so, do you see?” and he pushed Anatole’s head forward to meet the gap left by the collar, through which Matrësha’s brilliant smile was seen.

cases.sentence: — Ну, дай-то вам Бог, князь, счастья большого, — сказала Матреша, с своим ___.
cases.explain: «цыганским акцентом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “Well, Prince, may God give you great luck!” said Matrësha in her gypsy accent.

cases.sentence: — крикнул он, заматывая вокруг рук вожжи, и тройка понесла бить вниз по ___.
cases.explain: «Никитскому бульвару» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “Go!” he cried, twisting the reins round his hands, and the troyka tore down the Nikítski Boulevard.

cases.sentence: На ___ тройка зацепила карету, что-то затрещало, послышался крик, и тройка полетела по Арбату.
cases.explain: «Арбатской площади» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Tproo! Get out of the way! Hi! … Tproo! …” The shouting of Balagá and of the sturdy young fellow seated on the box was all that could be heard. On the Arbát Square the troyka caught against a carriage; something cracked, shouts were heard, and the troyka flew along the Arbát Street.

cases.sentence: Гаврило, огромный ___ Марьи Дмитриевны, встретил Анатоля.
cases.explain: «выездной лакей» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: He was met by Gavrílo, Márya Dmítrievna’s gigantic footman.

cases.sentence: Долохов ___ оттолкнул дворника и схватив за руку выбежавшего Анатоля, выдернул его за калитку и побежал с ним назад к тройке.
cases.explain: «последним усилием» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Dólokhov, after Anatole entered, had remained at the wicket gate and was struggling with the yard porter who was trying to lock it. With a last desperate effort Dólokhov pushed the porter aside, and when Anatole ran back seized him by the arm, pulled him through the wicket, and ran back with him to the troyka.
